posts.body:
Henlo people! I know I am new here, but that's exactly why I making questions. Ok, my problem here is...
I'm making a Horror RPG Games. Y'know, such as Mad Father, etc... The thing is, I wanna make an intro scene, which conforms an image zooming from in to out, and meanwhile the image is zooming, I'd like for a story to be told. (Y'know, like dialogue windows... Hope I'm explaining myself!)
Thing is, I'm totally new at these things. To be exact, I'm totally new at RPG Maker, so... I don't really have ANY IDEA on how it's done! I've tried looking through Internet and I've found something about using Common Events, but nothing clear.
I'm here to ask for help! Maybe there's some tutorial I could follow? Or someone who know about the topic (which would be extremely helpful!). Thanks!!! > <

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
LirioMB said:
Maybe there's some tutorial I could follow?
Click to expand...
If you're new to RPG Maker, there are plenty of tutorials that come up if you Google "rpg maker vx ace tutorial" - both video series on YouTube as well as articles on various sites.
You can also, generally, use tutorials from other makers - some specific things like the visual layout in the editor and a few specific features are different, but the general parts of how to edit information in the database and make events have been the same for years.
You should really do that first and make some little practice games as you do the tutorials so that you learn how to use RPG Maker before trying to worry about doing specific things you want in your game.

There are tons of tutorials on RPG Maker cutscenes, including on this site.
Cutscene Basics | The Official RPG Maker Blog
Cutscenes are a common occurrence in RPGs. In this tutorial we will look at ways to make cutscenes, as well as go over some tips and tricks to keep in mind while making them. We will demonstrate these by making a cutscene where Reid enters town, walks, then a dog and Kasey run past him and out...
www.rpgmakerweb.com

it is a bit mixed up due to forum updates that didn't keep the formatting, but it should still give you a guide to other tutorials and important facts.

but not that specific one!

all makerrs are too complex to effectively "learn by doing" - you'll always need a guide that points you on to make sure you got everything, or you'll scrap your dream game a year into development due to being frustrated with how bad your first tries at everything were, only then knowing how to do it better.
which is another reason why my tutorial suggests starting with a scrap project only to learn the basics without ever intending to comlete that one.
